title: Depolarization induces and hyperpolarization prevents tumour-like changes in tadpoles

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Depolarization induces and hyperpolarization prevents tumour-like changes in tadpoles

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In tadpoles, depolarizing a specific cell population is sufficient to cause metastatic-like transformation of normal melanocytes in genetically normal animals, while optogenetic or constitutive hyperpolarization prevents human oncogenes from inducing tumours.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: metastatic transformation of normal melanocytes can be achieved in genetically normal tadpoles simply by depolarizing a specific cell population (Lobikin et al., 2012), while, conversely, human oncogenes which normally induce tumors can be prevented from doing so simply by optogenetic or constitutive hyperpolarization (Chernet and Levin, 2013b, 2014; Chernet et al., 2015, 2016).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self”. Scope: Xenopus laevis tadpoles; melanocytes and human-oncogene-induced tumours

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.63

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The directional interventions and phenotypic outcomes are explicit and potentially discriminating. Published Xenopus evidence can resolve selected cases, but open raw records and controls needed to isolate voltage from channel-specific effects are uncertain.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare blinded melanocyte transformation and tumour outcomes after depolarizing or hyperpolarizing interventions versus matched controls, including oncogene-positive animals, and estimate sufficiency and prevention effects.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Channel manipulations may have non-voltage-specific effects.

Raw animal-level outcomes from the cited perturbations may not be public.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both arms are concrete Xenopus experiments, and the claim's scope is those tadpole systems, which the published measurements cover. The measurements are figures and summaries across several papers, so they can be compiled and cannot be reanalyzed at the animal level. Off-target physiology and single-program replication limit how decisively the existing record separates voltage from other effects of the reagents. The stated species and assay are partly covered; a clean reanalysis is not.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In genetically normal tadpoles, depolarize the stated cell population and score metastatic-like melanocyte behavior; in oncogene-bearing tadpoles, hyperpolarize by optogenetics or a constitutively open channel and score tumor incidence. Induction by depolarization and prevention by hyperpolarization would confirm the pair of results; either arm failing would refute that half.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Raw phenotype tables from the cited tadpole papers are not in a repository.

Depolarizing drugs and pump constructs have off-target effects.

Independent replication outside the original laboratory is thin.

data adequacy: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.84
